summary: SummitLedger: cascading fanout timeouts during EOD processing causing 5xx responses and truncated streaming — post-incident action plan
description:
Issue summary:
During SummitLedger's scheduled end-of-day (EOD) processing window (approx 02:00-03:00 UTC on 2026-03-10), a high-volume fanout of inference requests triggered cascading timeouts through the routing layer and autoscaler. This led to increased 5xx rates from the serving-runtime, truncated streaming completions for chat flows, and a temporary SLA exposure for SummitLedger (enterprise contract).

Impact:
- Multiple customer-facing APIs returned 500/502 errors and streaming responses were truncated mid-completion for ~28 minutes at peak.
- SummitLedger reported batch job replays and duplicate billing alerts from token accounting.
- Visible spike on customer dashboards and one escalation call with SummitLedger SRE/SPOC.

Timeline (high level):
- 02:01 UTC: Scheduled batch window begins.
- 02:04 UTC: Routing error rates increase; initial alert on gateway 5xx.
- 02:08 UTC: Autoscaler starts scaling but several GPU pools hit allocation failures (no free dedicated capacity).
- 02:12 UTC: Streaming truncation reports from SummitLedger; support ticket opened and oncall paged.
- 02:30 UTC: Mitigation (rate-limited fanout + temporary routing to fallback-small models) applied, error rate reduced.
- 02:35 UTC: Full routing configuration rollback and temporary quota increase for SummitLedger; streaming resume.
- 03:00 UTC: Incident declared over; monitoring resumed and ticket opened for post-incident follow-up.

Environment:
prod - us-east-1, SummitLedger routing policy: heavy fanout -> multi-model multiplexing with prefix caching enabled.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Simulate concurrent EOD job with 12k parallel synth requests using SummitLedger API key and same request prefix.
2) Use long-sequence prompts that trigger KV cache misses to force load on serving runtime.
3) Observe router queue growth, autoscaler allocation attempts and backend 5xx.

Observed logs / metrics (examples):
- gateway: 5xx rate from 0.2% to 8.6% between 02:04-02:20 UTC.
- router: queue depth spike to 17k, per-route tail latency P95 -> 4.3s.
- serving-runtime: "kernel selection failed" occasional traces coincident with memory pressure on quantized variants.
- billing/telemetry: replay window detected ~3k repeat requests for same batch job.

Temporary mitigations applied during incident:
- Enabled an emergency per-customer rate cap for SummitLedger (reduced concurrent fanout by 70%).
- Rerouted a percentage of traffic to smaller, non-quantized model variant to lower memory spikes.
- Increased soft quota for dedicated pool for 45 minutes to allow in-flight replays to drain.

Customer communications: SummitLedger notified via phone and #support escalation channel at 02:20 UTC; formal incident summary shared 03:10 UTC.

investigation_notes:
Initial root-cause hypothesis: coordinated high-fanout burst from a single customer producing large numbers of cold-kv cache misses, which caused high memory allocation on quantized serving kernels. Autoscaler attempted to spin up additional nodes, but allocation failures and allocation latency led to router queue growth and increased request retries.

Evidence collected:
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/company/summitledger/eod-20260310 (anonymized link included).
- Router logs: multiple allocation_timeout entries around 02:06-02:15 UTC.
- Kernel traces: intermittent kernel selection failures pinned to rwd-7b-v1-quant under long sequences.

Hypotheses tested and outcomes:
- H1 (Autoscaler config limits): rolled out temporary soft quota increase — reduced pressure, median latency improved. (Supported)
- H2 (Model quantization bug under long context): reproduced locally in staging with synthetic load — observed memory growth -> triggered patch to kernel selection. (Supported)
- H3 (Customer job misconfiguration): SummitLedger confirmed batch behavior (identical request prefixes); we recommended jitter and backoff. (Supported)
resolution:
Immediate fixes applied during incident: emergency rate cap, routing rollback, soft quota increase, and temporary routing to non-quantized variants. Post-incident technical fixes deployed in two releases:
- Routing/backpressure: PR #1428 added per-customer soft fanout limits and early-drop heuristics to the router (deployed 2026-03-12).
- Kernel selection safety: PR #891 adjusted heuristics to avoid quantized path under cold-kv conditions and included a memory guardrail (deployed 2026-03-13).

Customer remediation and follow-up:
- SummitLedger billing team will receive a credit for replayed requests for the impacted window (Finance lead assigned).
- Provided SummitLedger recommended runbook for scheduled EOD windows including suggested request jitter, per-job windowing, and pre-warming KV cache.
- Scheduled a postmortem review with SummitLedger on 2026-03-18 to review changes and long-term mitigation plan.

Current status: incident resolved in platform and customer environment. Monitoring rules updated (synthetic EOD test added) and platform mitigations in prod. Remaining follow-ups tracked below.
